history.period: Legendary/mythological; no datable temple structure documented
history.summary: NOTE: this CSV row is primarily a waterfall-pilgrimage site rather than a conventional temple; the adjacent Kapileshwar Shiva temple and Kapil Muni Ashram are part of the complex. Kapil Dhara is the first waterfall of the Narmada after its origin at Narmadakund (~6 km away): the river, joined by the Kapila and Erandi streams, plunges about 100 feet into a pool some 20-25 feet deep. Tradition holds that Sage Kapil meditated here, received divine illumination, and composed the Samkhya philosophy at this spot; one legend says he tried to halt the Narmada's westward (reverse) flow here. Pilgrims collect stones from the river, worshipped as Narmadeshwar/Shiva lingams, and revere the footprints of Lord Kapileshwar Shiva and Sage Kapil at the nearby ashram. About 100 steps down the trail is the smaller Doodh Dhara waterfall (~1 km further). Coordinates below are APPROXIMATE (verify).

name: Kapil Dhara Temple
town_description: Amarkantak is a pilgrim town in Anuppur district, Madhya Pradesh, on the Maikal hills at about 1,048 metres elevation. Revered as Tirtharaj, it is the source not only of the Narmada but also of the Sone and Johila rivers, and a traditional meeting point of the Vindhya and Satpura ranges. Dense sal forests surround the temple town.

travel.road: About 6 km from Amarkantak bus stand / Narmadakund; ~500 m walk from the parking area, concrete steps to the falls (lower steps reportedly washed away in floods — verify); Doodh Dhara is ~1 km further

visitor_information.best_time: September-January (post-monsoon); the falls are visitable all year
